title: Bookish & Biceps 4-Day
author: Ezra T.
desc:
Bookish and Biceps is a bodybuilding program that draws heavy inspiration from Beast Slayer, specifically the 4-day version. Cluster sets abound, alongside a split that is best described as LOWER - UPPER - FULL BODY - ARMS. 

I run this as a 4-day cycle and take rest days as needed. For me, this usually means every 8-9 days. Workouts average around 70 minutes in length. Volume for legs may seem low, but it is expected that you leave very little in the tank for what reps you do have. Have you ever tried to do a cluster set of front squats? No? So don't tell me that the program needs more quad volume. You are not doing them right. 

Add forearm/neck/lateral deltoid work as you see fit. This is enough stimulus for me, but may not be for you. I am also a believer in regular calf, ab, and trap work. Though this is a bodybuilding program, you will hopefully not find yourself lacking in strength anywhere.

ex.note: 2x Cluster sets with 30 seconds of rest, 3 minutes in between. Progress @ 10 confident reps.
Two minutes of rest. Go heavy. Goblet squats are great for training the balance required to front-squat well, which will be your primary quad exercise later within the week.
I count to three at the top of each rep. Calves can take a lot of haphazard punishment, but pauses are great for growth. 1 minute rest.
This lift is meant to be POWERFUL, but controlled. Reach failure, but do not allow yourself to use momentum to move the weight. You should be able to move your bodyweight.
3-4 sets of direct ab-work. Overload!
Two minutes of rest. You are practicing being unstable.
3-5x 6-10. 2 minutes of rest. Double progression.
3-5 sets of 6-10 reps. 2 minutes of rest. This movement comes from your elbows.

ss.note: I run this superset with 90 seconds of rest afterward. It's tough, but I think that the shrugs lead to a better chest isolation.

ex.note: More Face Pulls! This motion is hugely important for an aesthetic shoulder, even if you don't feel it. 1 minute rest.
1 minute rest. Lateral delts are important, or so I am told.
